Ausbildung: Dual vocational training: company + vocational school, 3½ years for the Elektroniker (ElekAusbV 2021).
Azubi / Auszubildende(r): A person in vocational training; always works under the supervision of an Elektrofachkraft (qualified electrician).
Berufsschule: The school-based part of the dual training system, taught according to learning fields (KMK framework curriculum).
Lernfeld: A teaching unit at the Berufsschule (vocational school), oriented around a typical customer order; 13 learning fields, 1 020 hours.
Gesellenprüfung (gestreckt): Final trade examination in two parts: Part 1 in the 4th half-year of training (30 %), Part 2 at the end (70 %).
Gesellenbrief: Certificate of having passed the journeyman examination; proof of qualification as an Elektroniker (electrician).
Kundenauftrag: The most important examination area in Part 2 (36 %): a 16-hour practical work task with a technical discussion.
Handwerkskammer (HWK): The competent body for training contracts, examinations and the master craftsman examination in the skilled trades.
Meister/-in: The highest qualification in the skilled trades (§ 45 HwO), required to run your own electrical business; DQR level 6.
Elektrofachkraft (EFK): A person with electrical training, experience and knowledge of standards who is permitted to work independently on electrical installations (DGUV V3).
Elektrotechnisch unterwiesene Person (Eu: A person instructed by an Elektrofachkraft (qualified electrician) for specific tasks; may only work under direction and supervision.
Netzbetreiber: The operator of the power grid; installs the Zähler (meter), seals it and maintains the Installateurverzeichnis (installer directory).
Installateurverzeichnis: A list kept by the Netzbetreiber (grid operator) of the companies allowed to work on the Hausanschluss (service connection) and meter position (§ 13 NAV).
Ausbildungsvergütung: Monthly pay during training; statutory minimum for 2026: €724 in the 1st year, collective-agreement rates are usually much higher.
Spannung (U): Electrical "pressure" between two points, unit volt (V). Domestic grid: 230 V / 400 V.
Strom / Stromstärke (I): Amount of charge per second flowing through a conductor, unit ampere (A).
Widerstand (R): A measure of how strongly a component or conductor limits the current, unit ohm (Ω).
Leistung (P): Work per second, P = U · I, unit watt (W).
Energie / Arbeit (W): Power times time, unit kilowatt-hour (kWh) – what the Zähler (meter) counts.
Ohmsches Gesetz: U = R · I – the relationship between voltage, resistance and current.
Wechselstrom / Wechselspannung: Current that periodically changes direction; in Europe 50 Hz, 230 V between the Außenleiter (line conductor) and the neutral conductor.
Drehstrom: Three alternating voltages offset by 120° (L1, L2, L3); 400 V between two Außenleiter (line conductors).
Außenleiter (L1, L2, L3): Live conductor ("phase"); colours brown, black, grey.
Neutralleiter (N): Return conductor, connected to the star point; colour blue.
Schutzleiter (PE): Conductor for protection against electric shock, carries no current in normal operation; colour green-yellow.
PEN-Leiter: Combined protective and neutral conductor in TN-C systems, up to the Hausanschluss (service connection); it is split on the Haupterdungsschiene (main earthing busbar).
Leiterfarben: Core identification according to DIN VDE 0293-308: L1 brown, L2 black, L3 grey, N blue, PE green-yellow.
Netzform (TN, TT, IT): The type of earthing of the grid and the equipment; in German residential buildings usually TN-C-S.
Erdung: Conductive connection to the earth, e.g. via the Fundamenterder (foundation earth electrode).
Fundamenterder: Strip steel or round steel in the concrete foundation used as an earth electrode; mandatory in new buildings.
Haupterdungsschiene (HES): The central earthing busbar in the service connection room; here the earth electrode, PE, PEN splitting and equipotential bonding are connected.
Potentialausgleich: Connection of all conductive parts (pipes, heating, steel) to the HES (main earthing busbar) so that no dangerous voltages can occur.
Querschnitt: Conductor cross-sectional area in mm²; determines current-carrying capacity and voltage drop (1.5 / 2.5 / 10 / 16 mm²).
Spannungsfall: Voltage loss along the cable due to its resistance; according to DIN 18015 it must generally not exceed 3 %.
Isolationswiderstand: Resistance of the insulation against PE, measured with 500 V DC; at least 1 MΩ.
Fehlerstrom: Current that flows to earth via an unintended path (enclosure, person); the RCD detects it.
Kurzschluss: A direct connection between conductors of different voltage; very high current, the LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breaker) trips immediately.
Überlast: A persistently excessive current caused by too many loads; the cable heats up and the LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breaker) trips with a time delay.
Schutzklasse (I, II, III): Classification of appliances by protection against electric shock: Class I with PE, Class II double-insulated, Class III low voltage.
Schutzart (IP): Protection of an enclosure against foreign objects and water, e.g. IP44 (protected against splashing water).
Leitungsschutzschalter (LS-Schalter): "Circuit-breaker fuse"; protects the cable against overload and short circuit, e.g. B16.
Auslösecharakteristik (B, C, D): Range of the magnetic trip unit of an LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breaker): B 3–5×, C 5–10×, D 10–20× rated current.
Nennstrom: The current a protective device may carry continuously, e.g. 16 A.
RCD / FI-Schutzschalter: Residual current protective device; trips on differential current, personal protection at IΔn = 30 mA.
Bemessungsdifferenzstrom (IΔn): The fault current at which an RCD trips at the latest; 30 mA for personal protection, 300 mA for fire protection.
RCD-Typ (A, F, B): The type of fault currents detected: A standard household, F frequency converters, B smooth DC fault currents (wallbox, PV).
RCBO: A combination of RCD and LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breaker) for a single circuit.
Schmelzsicherung: A fuse with a melting wire (Neozed, NH); must be replaced after tripping.
SLS-Schalter: Selective main-line circuit breaker in front of the Zähler (meter); acts as upstream protection and isolation point of the customer installation.
Selektivität: Only the protective device closest to the fault trips, not the upstream fuse.
Überspannungsschutz (SPD): Surge arrester against voltage spikes caused by lightning or switching operations; Type 1, 2, 3; mandatory in new buildings.
Prüftaste (T): A button on the RCD that simulates a fault current; press it monthly.
Hausanschlusskasten (HAK): The transfer point from the grid into the building with NH fuses; property of the Netzbetreiber (grid operator), sealed.
Hauptleitung: The unmetered cable from the HAK to the meter cabinet, e.g. 5×16 mm².
Zählerplatz / Zählerschrank: The location of the measurement according to VDE-AR-N 4100: busbar, SLS, meter field, distribution field, APZ.
Zähler (eHZ): Electronic household meter; installed and sealed by the metering point operator.
APZ: Lockable space for additional applications in the meter cabinet (smart meter gateway, control box).
Unterverteilung / Stromkreisverteiler: The "fuse box" of the apartment: main switch, SPD, RCDs, LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breakers), terminals.
Zuleitung: The cable from the meter cabinet to the sub-distribution board, e.g. NYM-J 5×10 mm².
Endstromkreis: A circuit from the LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breaker) to the loads (sockets, lighting, cooker).
Hauptschalter: Switches off the entire distribution board on all poles; the first step when isolating the installation.
Hutschiene: 35-mm mounting rail for DIN-rail mounted devices; 1 module (TE) = 18 mm.
Reiheneinbaugerät: A device for the Hutschiene (DIN rail): MCB, RCD, relay, timer.
Kammschiene / Phasenschiene: A plug-in busbar that connects several LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breakers) to the RCD.
Reihenklemme: A terminal on the Hutschiene (DIN rail) for N and PE conductors; N-splitting terminals per RCD group.
Aderendhülse: A metal ferrule on fine-stranded conductors for secure terminal connection.
NYM-J: Sheathed cable for fixed installation in dry and damp rooms; J = with green-yellow protective conductor.
Verteilerdose / Abzweigdose: A box in which cables are distributed using connector terminals.
Steckdose (Schuko): Socket outlet with protective contact (L, N and PE); in apartments behind a 30 mA RCD and LS B16.
Ausschaltung: Switching a light from one location; the Außenleiter (line conductor) is always the switched conductor.
Wechselschaltung: Switching a light from two locations; two two-way switches and two corresponding conductors.
Kreuzschaltung: Switching a light from three or more locations; an intermediate switch between two two-way switches.
Korrespondierende Leiter: The two conductors between two two-way switches (black, grey).
Geschalteter Leiter: The conductor from the switch to the light that carries voltage only when "on" (black).
Stromlaufplan: A circuit diagram in resolved (single-line) representation showing the functional relationship.
Installationsplan: A floor plan showing the positions of boxes, switches, lights and cables.
Fünf Sicherheitsregeln: Isolate · secure against re-energisation · verify absence of voltage · earth and short-circuit · cover adjacent parts (DIN VDE 0105-100).
Freischalten: Switching off the part of the installation on all poles before working on it – the first safety rule.
Spannungsfreiheit feststellen: Check all conductors with a two-pole voltage tester; test the tester before and afterwards.
Zweipoliger Spannungsprüfer: The only permitted device for verifying absence of voltage (DIN EN 61243-3).
Erstprüfung: Testing of every new installation before commissioning according to DIN VDE 0100-600: inspect, test, measure, record.
Prüfprotokoll: A document with all measured values, date and signature; part of the handover of the installation.
Schleifenimpedanz: The impedance of the fault loop; determines whether the LS-Schalter (miniature circuit breaker) trips safely in the event of a short circuit.
Drehfeld: The sequence of the line conductors L1–L2–L3; a clockwise (positive-sequence) field must be present at the Zähler (meter) and the cooker.
DGUV Vorschrift 3: Accident prevention regulation "Electrical installations and equipment"; governs who may work on and test them.
§ 13 NAV: Low-voltage connection ordinance: work behind the Hausanschluss (service connection) may only be carried out by registered installation companies.
VDE-AR-N 4100: Technical connection rule for low voltage: design of the Hausanschluss (service connection) and meter position.
DIN 18015: Standard for electrical installations in residential buildings: planning and minimum equipment (sockets, circuits).
DIN VDE 0100: Series of standards "Erection of low-voltage installations"; Part 410 protection against electric shock, Part 600 testing.
